Description: Ports in the 80NN range (e.g. 8000, 8001, etc.) are typically used by the SAP Internet Communication Manager (ICM) for handling non-TLS HTTP traffic. ICM is a core component in SAP NetWeaver systems, responsible for accepting incoming HTTP(S) requests and routing them to the appropriate internal SAP stack — usually ABAP, but sometimes Java in dual-stack systems.
Deployment Context: The 80NN ports are most commonly associated with ABAP stack deployments, particularly in systems exposing web-based access for SAP GUI, Fiori Launchpad, or SICF-enabled services. These ports are widely used for internal traffic, or externally via reverse proxies like SAP Web Dispatcher.
Access Behavior: ICM-bound ports in the 80NN range respond to HTTP requests and expose various endpoints under /sap/bc/, /sap/public/, and related paths. These services are commonly used for frontend user interaction, client connections, and web service access. In hardened setups, traffic to these ports may be proxied or upgraded to HTTPS (443NN).
Functional Capabilities: ICM over 80NN provides access to services such as SAP GUI for HTML (/sap/bc/gui/sap/its/webgui), Fiori Launchpad (/sap/bc/ui5_ui5/), and SICF-exposed web services (/sap/bc/srt/, /sap/public/...). It also serves dynamic content from BSP applications and Business Client interfaces. This port enables much of the interactive and service-based communication in ABAP environments.
Security Implications: Exposing the ICM over HTTP without TLS can lead to session hijacking, credential leakage, or unauthorized enumeration of SAP services. Additionally, misconfigured SICF services may expose sensitive data or lead to access control bypasses. Port 8000 and its siblings are often overlooked in external scans but can reveal significant attack surface in improperly segmented networks.
Detection Goals: This module will probe the 80NN range for SAP-specific responses by issuing GET and HEAD requests to common SAP endpoints. It will identify the presence of an ABAP stack, extract version and banner information, and log response data to aid in fingerprinting. It will also detect whether the ICM is directly exposed or accessed via a proxy.
Assessment Notes: If a port in the 80NN range is open and returns SAP-related content, the host is likely running an ABAP instance configured for web access. This is a critical component of user-facing SAP infrastructure and should be reviewed for exposure risks, service misconfigurations, and encryption policies.
